query: Republican voters Trump approval slipping poll

results.content:
The latest CNN poll showed Trump’s overall approval rating slipping to 34%, matching the career low he last saw in the aftermath of the Jan. 6 attack. The same survey showed the president struggling on issues across the board, and his backing among Republican voters has dropped to 78%, his worst-ever standing among members of his own party. [...] The latest Quinnipiac University poll showed Trump’s overall approval rating slipping to 32%, an all-time low, driven in large part by broad opposition to the war with Iran and the White House’s economic policies.
 The latest Associated Press poll also showed Trump’s overall approval rating slipping to 33%, for the same reasons as the other surveys.
results.title: As Trump’s approval rating reaches embarrassing depths, the GOP faces a difficult choice

results.content:
📉 An Economist/YouGov poll out Tuesday had Trump's approval rating among Republicans at a second-term low of 79 percent — a decline of 12 points from shortly after he took office.
   In that time, the percentage of Republicans who "strongly approve" of Trump's performance has dropped more precipitously —by 20 points (from 68 to 48 percent). [...] But Trump has dismissed bad polling for him as biased and "fake," and he routinely claims on Truth Social that his numbers are stronger than ever.

The bottom line:Trump's slipping poll numbers come with the post-Labor Day home stretch just weeks away — when voter perceptions become increasingly baked in.

results.title: Even some Republican voters sour on Trump

results.content:
Trump’s net approval rating among Republicans has dropped eight points since the groups’ survey last month, the Financial Times reported.

The poll comes as inflation cooled in July from June, but at 3.4%, it’s still higher than when Trump took office as the war with Iran has driven up fuel costs and disrupted the economy.

Meanwhile, Democrats have a five percentage-point advantage over Republicans in the upcoming midterm elections, according to the survey. [...] However, Republicans still approve of Trump’s job as president, according to the poll, with 76% approving his job performance, down slightly from 85% recorded by the pollster in June.
